summary: repmgr 4.0.0 through 5.5.0 is affected by an OS command injection vulnerability (CWE-78) in event...
description: repmgr 4.0.0 through 5.5.0 is affected by an OS command injection vulnerability (CWE-78) in event notifications. When event_notification_command is configured, repmgr substitutes the %a (node name), %c (connection string) and %d (details) placeholders into the command and runs it through the shell. %a and %c are inserted without escaping, and %d escapes only double quotes, so shell command substitution still works inside the quoting the documentation recommends. The node name and connection string come from node records in the repmgr.nodes table. An attacker with the credentials of a non-superuser repmgr database user can write a crafted node record and run OS commands, as the operating system user that runs repmgr or repmgrd (usually postgres), on other cluster nodes that process an event using these placeholders. The %a placeholder of failover_validation_command has the same flaw. Deployments whose repmgr database user is a superuser gain no new capability, because a superuser can already run OS commands, and deployments that do not use these placeholders are not affected. The issue is fixed in repmgr 5.5.1. After upgrading, operators must remove any quotes they placed around these placeholders, because a placeholder left inside double quotes is still open to command injection.

summary: proxygen's QPACK decoder enforced its size limit on a string literal in an encoder-stream...

The issue occurs regardless of the advertised QPACK dynamic table capacity, including when the dynamic table is disabled. This issue affects proxygen versions prior to v2026.11.09.00.

summary: In proxygen's HTTP/3 session, when a HEADERS block referenced QPACK dynamic table entries that...
description: In proxygen's HTTP/3 session, when a HEADERS block referenced QPACK dynamic table entries that had not yet been received, header decoding for that stream was paused, but the session continued to read the stream from the QUIC transport. The unread data bypassed the session's ingress buffer limit, returned flow-control credit to the peer, and was re-scanned in full on every read. With QPACK blocked streams enabled (the default), a remote, unauthenticated HTTP/3 peer could send a HEADERS block that references a dynamic table insert it never sends, followed by a continuous stream of data, causing memory growth until the request timed out and CPU usage that grows quadratically, leading to denial of service. This issue affects proxygen versions prior to v2026.11.09.00.

summary: The regcomp and regexec functions in the GNU C Library version 2.3 to version 2.44 may read freed...
description:
The regcomp and regexec functions in the GNU C Library version 2.3 to version 2.44 may read freed memory and free the same heap block twice when a memory allocation fails while a regular expression is compiled or matched.  The re_dfa_add_node (the NFA node table) and build_range_exp (bracket ranges) grow several arrays with consecutive realloc calls and store the new pointers only after all of them succeed.  When a later call fails, the pattern buffer keeps pointers to blocks that were already freed, and the error cleanup frees them again.  In regexec, the back-reference cache (match_ctx_add_entry) frees its array when a realloc fails but keeps the pointer, which is freed again on the error path.

An attacker does not need to supply a crafted regular expression: patterns large enough to grow these arrays are common.  The failure has to hit a specific allocation, though, so the issue can only be reached when the system is already under memory pressure.  An attacker who supplies the pattern or the subject string has little control over which allocation fails, so the expected impact is a crash of the process.  This issue affects all architectures and ABIs supported by the GNU C Library.

description:
Missing authorization in the JSON-RPC web services interface
of Extreme Networks Switch Engine (EXOS) allows an authenticated,
low-privileged (read-only) user to execute CLI show commands that are
restricted to that role through the command line interface. Successful
exploitation results in disclosure of sensitive information, including the
device configuration and the password hashes of local accounts. Configuration,
enable, and debug commands are not affected. Disclosed password hashes can be
attacked offline, and a weak password could lead to administrative access to
the device. This issue is fixed in Switch Engine 33.7.1-patch1-11,
33.1.100.133-patch1-9, and 32.7.4.15-patch1-11.








Extreme Networks would like to thank Toàn Lê (GitHub: https://github.com/toanln-cov) for responsibly disclosing this vulnerability and for working with our PSIRT team through coordinated disclosure.

summary: Calling the wide scanf family of functions (swscanf, fwscanf, wscanf, vswscanf, vfwscanf and...
description:
Calling the wide scanf family of functions (swscanf, fwscanf, wscanf, vswscanf, vfwscanf and vwscanf) with a %s or %[ conversion without the 'l' length modifier in the GNU C Library version 2.2 to version 2.44 writes an extra null byte one past the end of the destination array when the converted multibyte string and its terminating null byte exactly fill that array.

These conversions store each wide input character into the caller's char array as a multibyte sequence.  The conversion ends with the sequence that returns to the initial shift state, which also stores the terminating null byte, and the functions then append a second null byte.  A destination sized for the converted string and one terminator, as the C standard requires the caller to provide, is therefore written one byte past its end.  The out-of-bounds byte is always a null byte, which may corrupt adjacent data or crash the process.  An attacker who supplies the input can trigger the overflow with a string whose converted length exactly fills the destination.

The narrow scanf functions, the %ls and %l[ conversions into a wchar_t array, and the 'a' and 'm' allocation modifiers are not affected, and storing a wide scanf conversion into a narrow char array is uncommon.  This issue affects all architectures and ABIs supported by the GNU C Library.

summary: In Progress® Kendo® UI for jQuery versions prior to 2026.4.1111, kendo.init() compiles data-*...
description: In Progress® Kendo® UI for jQuery versions prior to 2026.4.1111, kendo.init() compiles data-* attribute values with new Function when an invalid JSON object is supplied. An attacker with low privileges who can control these attribute values can inject JavaScript that executes during declarative widget initialization when a user loads or interacts with an affected page. Successful exploitation can compromise the confidentiality and integrity of data accessible in the user's browser context. The issue was reported in version 2022.3.1109; the first affected release has not been established.

summary: An authorization bypass in Revive Adserver 6.0.0 through 6.0.8 allows an authenticated manager...
description: An authorization bypass in Revive Adserver 6.0.0 through 6.0.8 allows an authenticated manager restricted to one agency to access or modify resources belonging to another agency. Global input registration gives GET parameters precedence over POST parameters, while submitted administration forms use POST values. By supplying authorized object identifiers in the query string and different identifiers in the POST body, an attacker can cause permission checks and subsequent operations to target different objects. This permits unauthorized cross-agency changes, campaign ownership reassignment and disclosure of campaign and banner data. The regression was introduced in commit 156dee7bc3283c128f35e5a31bb305054cc8de1b and is fixed in Revive Adserver 6.0.9 by restoring POST precedence in global input registration.

summary: The WPML Multilingual CMS plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass via Race...
description: The WPML Multilingual CMS plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass via Race Condition in versions up to, and including, 4.9.7. This is due to the `process_iframe_request` function's language-per-domain SSO handler generating the cross-domain sign-in token via `wp_create_nonce('wpml_sso')` on the logout landing page, where the browser has already discarded its authentication cookies — so `wp_get_session_token()` returns an empty string and the token collapses to the shared anonymous nonce for the current 12-hour tick rather than a user-bound secret — and then storing it in the `wpml_sso_user_<token>_<sha256('wpml_sso'.$domain)>` transient mapped to the victim's `user_id` with no binding to the specific sign-out action or requesting client. Because an unauthenticated attacker can independently derive the identical token by triggering the logout confirmation flow on `wp-login.php?action=logout`, and because the `is_iframe_request()` gate conditions (the per-domain SSO `started` transient and domain-hash derived from the public constant `SSO_NONCE`) are fully computable within the 60-second `SSO_TIMEOUT` window, an unauthenticated attacker can submit the forged `wpml_sso_token_domain` parameter with a `wpml_user_signed_in` status to a secondary language-domain endpoint before the legitimate `wpml_user_signed_out` iframe fires, causing WordPress authentication cookies to be issued for the victim. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to gain access to accounts of users — including administrators — who are actively in the process of logging out during the race window.

summary: A flaw was found in openshift-ansible. The installer container's `run` script downloads and...
description: A flaw was found in openshift-ansible. The installer container's `run` script downloads and executes remote inventory and dynamic scripts without integrity verification. A remote attacker, by performing a Man-in-the-Middle (MITM) attack or compromising the HTTP server providing these scripts, could substitute an arbitrary executable. This malicious executable would then run with the installer's user ID (UID) and full cluster-provisioning privileges, leading to arbitrary code execution.

summary: A flaw was found in GIMP. The PSD thumbnail resource loader performs a BGR-to-RGB channel swap...
description: A flaw was found in GIMP. The PSD thumbnail resource loader performs a BGR-to-RGB channel swap with a fixed 3-byte stride and does not verify that the JPEG thumbnail is RGB. A crafted grayscale PSD thumbnail can cause a heap out-of-bounds read and write in the plug-in process, leading to a crash and potentially arbitrary code execution when the victim browses or opens the file.

description: A flaw was found in the DPDK nfp vDPA driver. Stack and heap buffers sized for a single queue pair can be overflowed when more virtqueues are configured, leading to a host crash or memory corruption.

description: A flaw was found in DPDK lib/vhost vhost-crypto. Integer overflow in chain length checks, and missing length checks on the RSA path, can overflow a host buffer in the vhost-crypto backend.

description: A flaw was found in DPDK lib/vhost. A guest with runt RX descriptors can underflow the copy length in vhost enqueue, causing a denial of service in a shared vhost backend such as OVS-DPDK.

summary: A flaw was found in libsoup. The soup_uri_decode_data_uri() function incorrectly treated base64...
description: A flaw was found in libsoup. The soup_uri_decode_data_uri() function incorrectly treated base64 data-URI payloads as NUL-terminated strings when calling g_base64_decode_inplace(). If the percent-decoded payload contained embedded NUL bytes, the decoded length could remain uninitialized and be used as the size of the returned GBytes. This can lead to an out-of-bounds read or application crash when processing a crafted data URI.

summary: A flaw was found in the DPDK vhost library. When handling a virtio indirect descriptor table, the...
description: A flaw was found in the DPDK vhost library. When handling a virtio indirect descriptor table, the host reads the table length more than once from guest memory and can allocate a host copy before validating that length. A guest that changes the length between those reads, or that supplies an out-of-range next index on a small host copy in the vDPA relay path, can cause the host vhost process to walk past the validated mapping or heap copy. That can crash or disrupt the vhost process. Out-of-bounds bytes are consumed as descriptor fields for GPA translation and are not returned to the guest as payload. This is a residual issue in the non-contiguous indirect descriptor copy path introduced as part of the CVE-2018-1059 fix.

summary: A heap-based buffer overflow was found in GIMP’s DirectDraw Surface (DDS) loader. When loading a...
description: A heap-based buffer overflow was found in GIMP’s DirectDraw Surface (DDS) loader. When loading a crafted DDS image, buffer sizes derived from width, height, and pitch can be computed using 32-bit arithmetic that overflows. The allocated buffer is too small for the amount of pixel data written through GEGL (CWE-787), following integer overflow in size calculations (CWE-190). This may allow heap corruption and, in the worst case, arbitrary code execution in the context of the GIMP process.

summary: A flaw was found in GIMP. When processing a specially crafted GIMPressionist preset file, the...
description: A flaw was found in GIMP. When processing a specially crafted GIMPressionist preset file, the plug-in does not properly validate vector indices before writing into fixed-size arrays. This can lead to an out-of-bounds write, corrupting memory. An attacker could exploit this by convincing a user to load a malicious preset file, potentially causing a crash or enabling arbitrary code execution.

summary: A stack-based buffer overflow flaw was found in fetchmail when built with NTLM support. A...
description: A stack-based buffer overflow flaw was found in fetchmail when built with NTLM support. A malicious or compromised mail server advertising NTLM authentication can send a crafted Type 2 challenge that causes fetchmail to write past a fixed stack buffer while building the NTLM authenticate response. This may lead to remote code execution depending on stack-frame layout, or to authentication failure or process termination under memory hardening.

summary: A flaw was found in cockpit-files. A low-privileged local user can exploit this vulnerability by...
description: A flaw was found in cockpit-files. A low-privileged local user can exploit this vulnerability by crafting a directory containing a symbolic link (symlink) and then using the privileged "Paste as owner" function. This allows for arbitrary file ownership changes outside the intended pasted directory, leading to a compromise of data integrity. In some cases, this could also lead to reduced confidentiality if the new ownership grants unauthorized read access. Exploitation requires user interaction to select a non-original owner during the paste operation.

summary: A flaw was found in flatpak-builder where Git hooks are not disabled when applying patch sources...
description: A flaw was found in flatpak-builder where Git hooks are not disabled when applying patch sources with use-git-am: true. An attacker who can provide a malicious source containing a Git post-applypatch hook can cause the hook to execute on the host during the build process, resulting in arbitrary code execution with the privileges of the user running flatpak-builder.

summary: A flaw was found in the file-psd plugin in GIMP. When generating a thumbnail preview for a...
description: A flaw was found in the file-psd plugin in GIMP. When generating a thumbnail preview for a specially crafted PSD (Photoshop Document) image file, an integer overflow occurs during the multiplication of values from an embedded JPEG header. This leads to an undersized heap allocation, resulting in a heap-based buffer overflow when the image data is decoded. This buffer overflow corrupts adjacent heap objects, allowing for a controlled memory write that can result in an application crash or arbitrary code execution.

summary: A flaw was found in GIMP. When processing a specially crafted lighting preset file, the Lighting...
description: A flaw was found in GIMP. When processing a specially crafted lighting preset file, the Lighting Effects filter does not properly validate the number of light sources. This can lead to an out-of-bounds write, corrupting memory. An attacker could exploit this by convincing a user to open a malicious preset file, potentially causing a crash or enabling arbitrary code execution.

description: A flaw was found in crun. When crun is built with libkrun and a container is started rootful with passt networking (krun.use_passt), crun can execute attacker-controlled payload from the container image with host root privileges. The issue is a regression in crun 1.29. It affects crun >= 1.29

summary: A flaw was found in libxml2 with Python bindings enabled. A remote attacker could exploit this...
description: A flaw was found in libxml2 with Python bindings enabled. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by providing a specially crafted XML document containing a Document Type Definition (DTD) with enumerated attribute values. This triggers a double-free error in the SAX attributeDecl callback handler, where a string is freed twice. This flaw can lead to a denial of service (DoS) due to a reproducible crash in Python applications using the libxml2 SAX bindings.

summary: A flaw was found in libsoup. A malicious HTTP/2 server or a Man-in-the-Middle (MITM) attacker can...
description: A flaw was found in libsoup. A malicious HTTP/2 server or a Man-in-the-Middle (MITM) attacker can exploit a heap use-after-free vulnerability in the HTTP/2 client implementation. This occurs when a GNOME application uploads a file using HTTP/2, and the server sends a GOAWAY frame while the file body is being read asynchronously. This can lead to memory corruption, potentially resulting in information disclosure or arbitrary code execution.

summary: A flaw was found in gnutls. When validating certificates, an oversized Subject Alternative Name ...
description: A flaw was found in gnutls. When validating certificates, an oversized Subject Alternative Name (SAN) could cause the validation process to incorrectly fall back to checking the Common Name (CN) field. This could allow a remote attacker to bypass proper certificate validation, potentially leading to spoofing or man-in-the-middle attacks.

summary: A vulnerability was found in libsoup's WebSocket frame parsing implementation. The library fails...
description: A vulnerability was found in libsoup's WebSocket frame parsing implementation. The library fails to validate length rules specified in RFC 6455 §5.5, which mandates that all WebSocket control frames (e.g., PING, PONG, CLOSE) contain a payload of 125 bytes or less. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can exploit this by sending a non-compliant, oversized control frame. Because the parser handles this protocol violation improperly instead of throwing an immediate connection termination error, it triggers a internal processing crash, resulting in a remote denial of service (DoS) for applications utilizing libsoup WebSockets.

summary: A flaw was found in gnutls. This vulnerability occurs because permitted name constraints were...
description: A flaw was found in gnutls. This vulnerability occurs because permitted name constraints were incorrectly ignored when previous Certificate Authorities (CAs) only had excluded name constraints. A remote attacker could exploit this to bypass critical name constraint checks during certificate validation. This bypass could lead to the acceptance of invalid certificates, potentially enabling spoofing or man-in-the-middle attacks against affected systems.

description: A flaw was found in BusyBox. An integer overflow occurs in the volume_id component when calculating buffer boundaries while probing filesystem metadata. An attacker can exploit this vulnerability by providing a specially crafted filesystem image on an attached storage device. When probed by utilities such as blkid, findfs, or mount, the application crashes, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS) that prevents the system from resolving or mounting storage devices.
